note: Local policy; qualify changes with independent checks.
forbiddenEdges: the generator never sees the frozen tests (DEC-72, L-16)
the test writer never sees the kernel; it writes from the contract
reviewers judge the artefact through its interface and the request, not the generator's code
the generator never reads reviewer criteria (honesty rule)

kindProcedures.kernel: Fixed procedure for kernel atoms: write AssemblyScript with exported pure functions over f64/i32/bool only, no imports, no persistent state; refuse invalid input with unreachable(). Prefix every private helper, constant or table with your atom id in camelCase (for example kCharge_densityKgM3) so that kernel parts can be concatenated into one module without collisions; never define a helper with a generic name. Compile-check each output file with: {asc} /out/<file> --runtime stub -O3 --noAssert -o /tmp/check.wasm --textFile /tmp/check.wat (it must report no diagnostics). Export exactly the functions the interface assigns to you.
kindProcedures.tests: Fixed procedure for test atoms: the output is a JSON array in the gate format: [{"name": "...", "fn": "exportName", "args": [numbers], "expect": number|boolean, "tol": absolute tolerance (required for non-integer expectations), "expectError": true (for calls that must refuse)}]. The file is parsed with JSON.parse and the arguments are passed to the WebAssembly export: write 1e999 for +Infinity, -1e999 for -Infinity, and the string "NaN" for NaN (the runner coerces it); never write the words Infinity or NaN bare, and never write null. Derive expectations from the contract and the interface only; show the arithmetic in the test name where it helps a reader. Include the request's own case, at least one boundary, and refusals for every refused input class.
kindProcedures.glue: Fixed procedure for glue atoms: the output is one JSON object valid against the closed glue schema below, complete for the exports assigned to you. Shape: {"id": "{needId}", "assumption": "...", "question": "...", "notes": "..." (optional), "exports": [{"name", "label", "headline" (optional), "args": [{"name", "kind": "number|integer|boolean|code", "unit", "label" (optional), "codes" (required when kind is code: {"1": "meaning"}), "range" (optional, words)}], "result": {"kind", "unit", "precision" (integer 0..6, required for number), "codes" (required for code results), "labels": {"true": "...", "false": "..."} (required for boolean results)}}], "traps": [{"fn", "when", "message"}]}. No other keys anywhere: args never carry labels or precision; results never carry range. Every export you describe needs one arg entry per argument; every export that refuses input needs a trap entry whose message says why and what to supply. The schema itself: {glueSchema}
kindProcedures.compose: Fixed procedure for the compose atom: run exactly `node {helper} --id {needId} --in /in --out /out --work /work --gate {gate}`. It assembles /work/{needId} (CONTRACT.md from the contract atom, tests.json merged from the test atoms, frozen before any code; kernel.ts concatenated from the kernel atoms; glue.json merged from the glue atoms), runs the fixed gates G1-G7 and copies kernel.wasm, CONTRACT.md, tests.json, glue.json and gates.json to /out. If it fails to compile because two kernel parts declare the same private name, edit /work/{needId}/kernel.ts to drop exact duplicate private declarations or rename one private helper (never an export, never a formula, never a constant's value), run `node {gate} run /work/{needId}` again, and copy the five outputs to /out yourself (result.json becomes gates.json). Never edit tests.json or CONTRACT.md: they are frozen. If a gate still fails, copy the outputs anyway with gates.json showing the failure, and finish.
kindProcedures.review: Fixed procedure for review atoms: judge from the request and the artefact's interface, contract, glue and gate record only; you never see the kernel source. Output one JSON object: {"persona": "<your frame>", "verdict": "accept" | "accept-with-change" | "reject", "change": "the one change named (accept-with-change) or the reason (reject), else null", "reasons": ["..."]}. accept = usable as returned; accept-with-change = one named change would make it usable; reject = it answers a question that was not asked, its default assumption is unsafe or implausible for the field, or its output cannot be acted on.
kindProcedures.compose-draft: Fixed procedure for the compose atom: run exactly `node {helper} --id {needId} --in /in --out /out --work /work --gate {gate}`. It assembles /work/{needId} (CONTRACT.md from the contract atom, tests.json merged from the test atoms, frozen before any code; kernel.ts concatenated from the kernel atoms; glue.json merged from the glue atoms), runs the fixed gates G1-G7 and copies kernel.wasm, CONTRACT.md, tests.json, glue.json and gates.json to /out. If it fails to compile because two kernel parts declare the same private name, edit /work/{needId}/kernel.ts to drop exact duplicate private declarations or rename one private helper (never an export, never a formula, never a constant's value), run `node {gate} run /work/{needId}` again, and copy the five outputs to /out yourself (result.json becomes gates.json). Never edit tests.json or CONTRACT.md: they are frozen. If a gate still fails, copy the outputs anyway with gates.json showing the failure, and finish.
kindProcedures.repair: Fixed procedure for the repair atom: among your inputs, failures.json lists the tests the draft composition failed (name, fn, args, expected, got); an empty list means every gate passed. If it is empty, copy every kernel part to /out unchanged under its original filename and write /out/repair-notes.md saying no gate failed. Otherwise, for each failing test decide from the contract, the interface and the data whether the kernel or the expectation is wrong: where the kernel is wrong, fix the part file (keep every export, keep the helper prefixes, no imports, refusals via unreachable()); where the expectation is wrong, leave the kernel and write exactly why in repair-notes.md with the arithmetic. Never edit tests or the contract (they are frozen and you do not have them). Compile-check each part with {asc} <file> --runtime stub -O3 --noAssert -o /tmp/check.wasm --textFile /tmp/check.wat. Write every part to /out under the output filename declared for it, plus repair-notes.md. One round only.
kindProcedures.direct: Fixed procedure for the direct worker (one worker does the whole capability; the incumbent loop-0 protocol): (1) In /work/{needId}/ write CONTRACT.md (what is computed; the assumption taken wherever the request leaves a fact open; the one question that resolves it; which inputs are refused) and tests.json (a JSON array in the gate format: [{"name", "fn", "args": [numbers], "expect": number|boolean, "tol": absolute tolerance for non-integers, "expectError": true for refusals}]; write 1e999 for +Infinity, -1e999 for -Infinity, the string "NaN" for NaN; include the request's own case, boundaries and refusals). (2) Freeze them before any code: node {gate} freeze /work/{needId}. Never edit CONTRACT.md or tests.json after this. (3) Write /work/{needId}/kernel.ts (AssemblyScript, exported pure functions over f64/i32/bool, no imports, refusals via unreachable()) and /work/{needId}/glue.json (closed schema below; id must be "{needId}"). (4) Run node {gate} run /work/{needId}; on failure repair kernel.ts and glue.json only, at most 3 repair rounds. (5) Copy kernel.wasm, kernel.wat, kernel.ts, CONTRACT.md, tests.json, glue.json and frozen.sha256 from /work/{needId}/ to /out/, and copy /work/{needId}/result.json to /out/gates.json. Finish. Glue schema: {glueSchema}
kindProcedures.asset: Fixed procedure for asset atoms (3D assets for the media kit): build with the CPU wrapper `blender-cpu -t 8 -P <script> -- <args>` (it is on PATH; it adds -b, --factory-startup and --python-exit-code 1). Read sources and references only from the read-only binds named in your inputs; write every declared output under /out. Never write into a bind, never use a GPU, never fetch from the network. Run the atom's own check or gate command before finishing, and write its result to /out next to the asset. If the check fails, keep the outputs and the failing result; do not hide failures.

repairSees: failing tests only (name, fn, args, expected, got); one round; tests and contract stay frozen
